In a diploid organism, two linked genes lie 20 map units apart on the same chromosome. An individual that is heterozygous at both loci, with the dominant alleles in coupling (AB/ab), is testcrossed to a homozygous recessive partner. Interference between crossovers in this interval is ignored. Among 1,000 offspring of the testcross, how many are expected to show the dominant phenotype at the first locus and the recessive phenotype at the second, and what fraction of all offspring are recombinant?

Compound 3, the larger of the two, is treated with excess ethylmagnesium bromide in dry diethyl ether followed by aqueous ammonium chloride to give compound 5. 1	# ADR-0024: the repository's layout
     2	
     3	**Status:** accepted, 2026-10-14, by the owner. Item 1 superseded in part by
     4	[ADR-0025](0025-the-engine-image.md): the layout gains a `Dockerfile` at the root; and by
     5	[ADR-0028](0028-ci-without-a-card.md): it gains `.github/workflows/`.
     6	**Revisit when:** a second model architecture is added ([ADR-0006](0006-scope.md)), or the scaffold
     7	(P49) finds the layout does not build.
     8	
     9	## Context
    10	
    11	- [ADR-0022](0022-two-processes-python-and-cpp.md) splits the engine into a Python front end, a Python control plane
    12	  and a C++20 core behind one C ABI. Kernels are OpenCL C and share layouts with the core through headers in the C
    13	  subset both accept ([ADR-0003](0003-kernel-language.md)).
    14	- The kernels read the step plan, the flags and the page table in place, in host memory
    15	  ([DESIGN.md, sections 2 and 4](../DESIGN.md#2-a-request-end-to-end)). The KV layout has one definition.
    16	- The engine runs one model architecture, `qwen4exp` (ADR-0006). Most of the code does not depend on it: Level Zero,
    17	  memory, signalling, timing, the CPU's expert products, the scheduler, the front end. Some does: the layer program,
    18	  its kernels, the KV layout, the kinds of sequence state, the n-gram reader, the split rules and the memory plan's
    19	  numbers.
    20	
    21	## Decision
    22	
    23	1. The layout:
    24	
    25	   ```
    26	   CMakeLists.txt, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .python-version
    27	   cmake/                   the ocloc rule, the ggml fetch
    28	   include/engine_api.h     the C ABI
    29	   shared/                  headers compiled as both C++20 and OpenCL C 3.0: step plan, flags, quant blocks
    30	   core/                    C++20: api/ ze/ mem/ sync/ load/ step/ cpu/ timing/ tests/
    31	     models/qwen4exp/       layer program, state kinds, n-gram reader, KV layout
    32	   kernels/                 OpenCL C: include/ (the builtin wrappers), quant/ sample/ exchange/, module table
    33	     models/qwen4exp/       DeltaNet, attention, indexer, hyper-connections, norms
    34	   protocol.py              the line protocol between the two processes
    35	   frontend/                the process that is started, by hand or by a proxy such as llama-swap
    36	   engine/                  the control plane: scheduler, admission, seqstate/, memory plan, timing
    37	     api/                   ctypes mirror (abi.py), native, mock, reference
    38	     models/qwen4exp/       tensor table, split rules, state kinds, memory-plan numbers
    39	   tools/                   the attach tool and other engine tools
    40	   tests/<level>/           one folder per TESTING.md level; tests/<level>/qwen4exp/ for the model's own
    41	   ```
    42	
    43	2. No path carries the project's name. Python packages are top-level. The C ABI's symbols carry the prefix
    44	   `engine_`, because `open`, `poll` and `close` clash with libc.
    45	3. Code that depends on the model architecture lives in `models/<arch>/` under `core/`, `kernels/` and `engine/`.
    46	   `<arch>` is the GGUF architecture name. Code outside `models/` does not name the model.
    47	4. No model interface (base class, registry) until a second architecture exists. The shared code is then drawn
    48	   from the two.
    49	5. `shared/` holds only headers that compile as both C++20 and OpenCL C 3.0. A build step compiles each one both
    50	   ways.
    51	6. `engine/api/abi.py` mirrors `engine_api.h` by hand. A level-1 test checks every struct's size and field offsets
    52	   against a table the core exports.
    53	7. `frontend/` never imports `engine/`; a level-1 test checks the imports. Both use `protocol.py`.
    54	
    55	## Options not chosen
    56	
    57	- A top-level folder or package named after the project: one more level in every path, and nothing gained.
    58	- Model code beside generic code (the layer program in `step/`, state kinds in `seqstate/`): separating them for a

   161	    if max_tokens < 1:
   162	        raise BadRequest("max_tokens must be at least 1")
   163	    if max_tokens > room:

   171	class _StopStrings:
   172	    """Holds back content that could be the start of a stop string."""
   173	
   174	    def __init__(self, stops: Sequence[str]) -> None:
   175	        self.stops = [s for s in stops if s]
   176	        self.pending = ""
   177	
   178	    def push(self, text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
   179	        if not self.stops:
   180	            return text, None
   181	        self.pending += text
   182	        hits = [(i, s) for s in self.stops if (i := self.pending.find(s)) >= 0]
   183	        if hits:
   184	            i, s = min(hits)
   185	            out, self.pending = self.pending[:i], ""
   186	            return out, s
   187	        hold = 0
   188	        for s in self.stops:
   189	            for n in range(min(len(s) - 1, len(self.pending)), 0, -1):
   190	                if s.startswith(self.pending[-n:]):
   191	                    hold = max(hold, n)
   192	                    break
   193	        out = self.pending[: len(self.pending) - hold]
   194	        self.pending = self.pending[len(out) :]
   195	        return out, None
   196	
   197	    def flush(self) -> str:
   198	        out, self.pending = self.pending, ""
   199	        return out

   209	    cached = 0

   212	        return list(parser.feed(text))
   213	
   214	    async with aclosing(engine.generate(prompt.ids, max_new, request.settings, prompt.images)) as events:
   215	        async for event in events:
   216	            match event:
   217	                case protocol.Resume(reused=reused):
   218	                    cached = reused
   219	                case protocol.Tokens(ids=ids):
   220	                    generated += len(ids)
   221	                    text = detok.push([i for i in ids if i not in model.stop_ids])
   222	                    for piece in pieces(text):
   223	                        if isinstance(piece, Content):
   224	                            out, hit = stops.push(piece.text)
   225	                            if out:
   226	                                yield Content(out)
   227	                            if hit is not None:
   228	                                yield End(Finish.STOP_STRING, len(prompt.ids), generated, cached, stop_string=hit)
   229	                                return
   230	                        else:
   231	                            yield piece
   232	                case protocol.Done(finish=finish, reused=reused, prompt_ms=prompt_ms, decode_ms=decode_ms):
   233	                    cached = reused or cached
   234	                    try:
   235	                        tail = pieces(detok.flush()) + list(parser.finish())
   236	                    except ToolCallError as exc:
   237	                        yield End(Finish.ERROR, len(prompt.ids), generated, cached, error=str(exc))
   238	                        return
   239	                    for piece in tail:
   240	                        if isinstance(piece, Content):
   241	                            out, hit = stops.push(piece.text)
   242	                            if out:
   243	                                yield Content(out)
   244	                            if hit is not None:
   245	                                yield End(Finish.STOP_STRING, len(prompt.ids), generated, cached, stop_string=hit)
   246	                                return
   247	                        else:
   248	                            yield piece
   249	                    if rest := stops.flush():
   250	                        yield Content(rest)

   252	                        protocol.Finish.STOP: Finish.STOP,
   253	                        protocol.Finish.LENGTH: Finish.LENGTH,
   254	                        protocol.Finish.CANCEL: Finish.CANCEL,
   255	                    }[finish]
   256	                    if why is Finish.STOP and parser.calls:
   257	                        why = Finish.TOOL_CALLS
   258	                    yield End(why, len(prompt.ids), generated, cached, prompt_ms=prompt_ms, decode_ms=decode_ms)
   259	                    return
   260	                case protocol.Error(message=message):
   261	                    yield End(Finish.ERROR, len(prompt.ids), generated, cached, error=message)
   262	                    return
   263	                case _:
   264	                    pass

   267	async def collect(pieces: AsyncIterator[Piece | End]) -> Result:
   268	    result = Result()

   273	            case Content(text=t):
   274	                result.content.append(t)
   275	            case ToolCall():
   276	                result.calls.append(piece)
   277	            case End():

1	"""The line protocol between the front end and the engine process (DESIGN.md, sections 1 and 2).
     2	
     3	One message per line, ASCII, fields separated by single spaces. Every line about a request carries its id, so the
     4	tokens of several requests can be told apart (ADR-0010, item 6). The lines follow Strata's
     5	(spec/STRATA_DECODE.md, section 10), with the request id added and the fields Strata's single-sequence engine needed
     6	for its caches left out.
     7	
     8	Front end to engine:
     9	
    10	    IMG <rid> <first> <grid_h> <grid_w> <frames> <path>
    11	    GEN <rid> <max_new> [key=value ...] <id,id,...>
    12	    STOP <rid>
    13	    SLEEP [<drain_ms>]
    14	    WAKE
    15	    QUIT
    16	
    17	A request's images come before its GEN, one IMG line each, in prompt order; a video is one IMG line per pair of its
    18	frames, `frames` 2. `path` names a file of the front end's (a memfd, as /proc/<pid>/fd/<n>) holding the image's
    19	patches, which the engine reads when it reads the line.
    20	
    21	Engine to front end:
    22	
    23	    INFO key=value ...
    24	    READY <max_context> <slots>
    25	    ASLEEP <ms>
    26	    RESUME <rid> <reused>
    27	    PP <rid> <reached> <prompt> <ms>
    28	    T <rid> <id>[,<id>...]
    29	    DONE <rid> <generated> <prompt> <prompt_ms> <decode_ms> <finish> <reused>
    30	    ERR <rid|-> <message>
    31	
    32	`ERR -` is about the engine, not one request, and the engine exits after it.
    33	
    34	`SLEEP` gives the cards back (ADR-0032). The engine refuses its queued requests and every later `GEN` with
    35	`ERR <rid>`, lets the running ones go on for up to `drain_ms` (default 0), ends the rest with finish `cancel`, frees
    36	its memory on the cards and answers `ASLEEP` with the time from the command. `WAKE` loads the cards again and answers
    37	`INFO` and `READY`, as at the start. `QUIT` ends the engine, awake or asleep.
    38	"""

   121	    @classmethod

   123	        """Unknown keys are skipped, as Strata's engine does, so an older engine reads a newer front end's lines."""
   124	        types = {f.name: f.type for f in fields(cls)}
   125	        values: dict[str, int | float] = {}

   127	            key, sep, text = pair.partition("=")

   129	                raise ProtocolError(f"setting without '=': {pair!r}")

1	"""The scheduler: admission, step plans and the requests' lives (ADR-0017; DESIGN.md, sections 2 and 4).
     2	
     3	Each tick it admits what fits, builds one step plan of changes, submits it, and turns the core's events into
     4	protocol lines. The rules, from ADR-0017:
     5	
     6	- Prompt work is scheduled by time. While a request is writing, a prompt step aims at `prompt_budget_ms`, sized by
     7	  the cost model; after it, decode is owed `decode_share` of its time before the next prompt step. With nobody
     8	  writing, a prompt takes whole chunks.
     9	- Short prompts are packed into one step, shortest first. A prompt passed over `max_passes` times goes first.
    10	- One producer per shared prefix: a request whose prompt starts with a prefix another request will checkpoint waits
    11	  for that checkpoint, holding no slot and no pages, unless it has the higher priority.
    12	- Checkpoints are taken where the model's rule puts them; a prompt span ends at each one.
    13	
    14	The core keeps decoding between plans, so a plan is built only when something changes.
    15	"""

   124	class Scheduler:
   125	    def __init__(

   127	        engine: Engine,

   130	        checkpoint_rule: CheckpointRule = every_16k,
   131	        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
   132	    ) -> None:

   139	        self.cost = CostModel.initial()
   140	        self.waiting: list[Request] = []
   141	        self.by_rid: dict[int, Request] = {}
   142	        self.by_slot: dict[int, Request] = {}
   143	        self.owed_ms = 0.0
   144	        self.spans_in_flight: dict[int, int] = {}
   145	        self._serial = 0

   147	    @property
   148	    def idle(self) -> bool:
   149	        return not self.by_rid

   151	    # Commands.
   152	
   153	    def add(self, gen: protocol.Gen, priority: int = 0, images: tuple[Image, ...] = ()) -> list[protocol.Event]:
   154	        if gen.rid in self.by_rid:
   155	            return [protocol.Error(gen.rid, "request id already in use")]
   156	        if gen.max_new < 1:
   157	            return [protocol.Error(gen.rid, "max_new must be at least 1")]
   158	        if len(gen.prompt) + gen.max_new > self.facts.max_context:
   159	            return [
   160	                protocol.Error(
   161	                    gen.rid,
   162	                    f"prompt ({len(gen.prompt)}) plus max_new ({gen.max_new}) exceeds the context "
   163	                    f"({self.facts.max_context})",
   164	                )
   165	            ]
   166	        if (problem := self._image_problem(gen.prompt, images)) is not None:
   167	            return [protocol.Error(gen.rid, problem)]
   168	        r = Request(gen.rid, gen.prompt, gen.max_new, gen.settings.with_defaults(), self.clock(), priority)
   169	        r.images = images
   170	        r.key = prefix_key(gen.prompt, images)
   171	        self.by_rid[r.rid] = r
   172	        self.waiting.append(r)
   173	        return []
   174	
   175	    def _image_problem(self, prompt: tuple[int, ...], images: tuple[Image, ...]) -> str | None:
   176	        if not images:
   177	            return None
   178	        if not self.facts.image_tokens_max:
   179	            return "this engine reads no images"
   180	        end = 0
   181	        for i, im in enumerate(images):
   182	            try:
   183	                im.check()
   184	            except ValueError as exc:
   185	                return f"image {i}: {exc}"
   186	            if im.tokens > self.facts.image_tokens_max:
   187	                return f"image {i} has {im.tokens} tokens, more than {self.facts.image_tokens_max}"
   188	            if im.first < end or im.first + im.tokens > len(prompt):
   189	                return f"image {i}: its tokens at {im.first} are out of order or past the prompt"
   190	            end = im.first + im.tokens
   191	        return None
   192	
   193	    def cancel(self, rid: int) -> list[protocol.Event]:
   194	        r = self.by_rid.get(rid)
   195	        if r is None:
   196	            return []
   197	        if r.phase is Phase.WAITING:
   198	            self.waiting.remove(r)
   199	            del self.by_rid[rid]
   200	            return [protocol.Done(rid, 0, len(r.prompt), 0.0, 0.0, protocol.Finish.CANCEL)]
   201	        r.cancelled = True
   202	        return []

   204	    def refuse_waiting(self, message: str) -> list[protocol.Event]:
   205	        """Every request not yet admitted ends with an error; the admitted ones go on."""
   206	        out: list[protocol.Event] = []
   207	        for r in list(self.waiting):
   208	            self.waiting.remove(r)
   209	            del self.by_rid[r.rid]
   210	            out.append(protocol.Error(r.rid, message))
   211	        return out

   213	    # The tick.
   214	
   215	    def tick(self, timeout_s: float) -> list[protocol.Event]:
   216	        out: list[protocol.Event] = []
   217	        self._admit(out)
   218	        self._plan()
   219	        for event in self.engine.wait(timeout_s):
   220	            self._handle(event, out)
   221	        return out

   223	    def _producer_for(self, r: Request, have: int) -> int | None:
   224	        """The request r should wait for: one that will checkpoint a prefix of r's prompt longer than `have`, or
   225	        has one in progress. -1 for a checkpoint whose producer has moved on but which the core has not answered."""
   226	        for p in self.by_rid.values():
   227	            if p is r or p.phase is Phase.WAITING or p.priority < r.priority:
   228	                continue
   229	            for position, _ in p.marks:
   230	                if have < position < len(r.key) and p.key[:position] == r.key[:position]:
   231	                    return p.rid
   232	        for ck in self.state.checkpoints:
   233	            n = len(ck.tokens)
   234	            if not ck.ready and have < n < len(r.key) and r.key[:n] == ck.tokens:
   235	                return -1
   236	        return None

   238	    def _admit(self, out: list[protocol.Event]) -> None:
   239	        self.waiting.sort(key=lambda r: (-r.priority, r.arrived))
   240	        for r in list(self.waiting):
   241	            best = self.state.checkpoints.longest_prefix(r.key)
   242	            producer = self._producer_for(r, len(best.tokens) if best else 0)
   243	            if producer is not None:
   244	                r.waiting_for = producer
   245	                continue
   246	            r.waiting_for = None
   247	            admission = self.state.plan_admission(r.key, r.max_new)
   248	            if admission is None:
   249	                break
   250	            self._flush_drops()
   251	            seq = self.state.admit(admission, r.key, r.max_new)
   252	            s = r.settings
   253	            try:
   254	                self.engine.admit(
   255	                    seq.slot,
   256	                    SlotSettings(
   257	                        s.temperature,
   258	                        s.top_p,
   259	                        s.top_k,
   260	                        s.min_p,
   261	                        s.penalty_last_n,
   262	                        s.penalty_repeat,
   263	                        s.penalty_freq,
   264	                        s.penalty_present,
   265	                        s.seed,
   266	                        r.max_new,
   267	                    ),
   268	                    r.prompt,
   269	                    r.images,
   270	                )
   271	            except EngineError as exc:
   272	                self.state.release(seq.slot)
   273	                self.waiting.remove(r)
   274	                del self.by_rid[r.rid]
   275	                out.append(protocol.Error(r.rid, str(exc)))
   276	                continue

   279	            r.slot = seq.slot
   280	            r.next_pos = r.done_pos = r.reused = seq.start
   281	            r.t_admit = self.clock()

   284	            if admission.checkpoint is not None:
   285	                self.engine.restore(seq.slot, admission.checkpoint.id)

   288	    def _flush_drops(self) -> None:
   289	        for checkpoint_id in self.state.drops:
   290	            self.engine.drop(checkpoint_id)
   291	        self.state.drops.clear()
   292	
   293	    def _plan(self) -> None:
   294	        plan = StepPlan(self._serial + 1)
   295	        for r in self.by_slot.values():
   296	            if r.cancelled and not r.stop_sent:
   297	                plan.stop.append(r.slot)
   298	                r.stop_sent = True
   299	            elif r.phase is Phase.DECODE:
   300	                self._grow_ahead(r, len(r.prompt) + r.generated)
   301	        marks = self._prompt_spans(plan)
   302	        plan.pages = self.state.take_changes(MAX_PAGE_CHANGES)
   303	        if plan.empty:
   304	            return
   305	        self._serial = plan.serial
   306	        self.engine.submit(plan)
   307	        self.state.submitted()
   308	        for span in plan.prompt:
   309	            self.spans_in_flight[span.slot] = self.spans_in_flight.get(span.slot, 0) + 1
   310	        for r, position, kept in marks:
   311	            ck = self.state.checkpoint(r.slot, position, kept)
   312	            self._flush_drops()
   313	            if ck is not None:
   314	                self.engine.checkpoint(r.slot, ck.id)
   315	        self._flush_drops()

   317	    def _grow_ahead(self, r: Request, used: int) -> None:
   318	        """Pages for the cells after the first `used`: at least `decode_lookahead`, then `decode_batch` more."""
   319	        o = self.options
   320	        if self.state.sequences[r.slot].cells < used + o.decode_lookahead:
   321	            self.state.grow(r.slot, used + o.decode_lookahead + o.decode_batch)
   322	
   323	    def _prompt_spans(self, plan: StepPlan) -> list[tuple[Request, int, bool]]:
   324	        """Fill the plan's prompt spans. Returns the checkpoints to take after it."""
   325	        if self.spans_in_flight:
   326	            return []
   327	        candidates = [
   328	            r for r in self.by_slot.values() if r.phase is Phase.PREFILL and r.remaining > 0 and not r.cancelled
   329	        ]
   330	        if not candidates:
   331	            return []
   332	        writing = any(r.phase is Phase.DECODE for r in self.by_slot.values())
   333	        if not writing:
   334	            self.owed_ms = 0.0
   335	        elif self.owed_ms > 0:
   336	            return []
   337	        o = self.options
   338	        budget = min(o.chunk_rows, self.cost.rows_within(o.prompt_budget_ms)) if writing else o.chunk_rows
   339	        candidates.sort(key=lambda r: (r.passes < o.max_passes, r.remaining, r.arrived))
   340	        marks: list[tuple[Request, int, bool]] = []
   341	        chosen: set[int] = set()
   342	        for r in candidates:
   343	            if budget <= 0 or len(plan.prompt) >= MAX_PROMPT_SPANS:
   344	                break
   345	            rows = min(r.remaining, budget, r.next_mark() - r.next_pos)
   346	            seq = self.state.sequences[r.slot]
   347	            room = MAX_PAGE_CHANGES - self.state.pending_changes
   348	            fits = (len(seq.pages) + room) * PAGE_CELLS - r.next_pos
   349	            rows = min(rows, fits)
   350	            if rows <= 0:

1	"""The KV page pool: physical page ids, reference counts, free lists and reservations (DESIGN.md, section 4).
     2	
     3	Only integers live here. The bytes are the core's; the page ids are the same on both cards, so one table serves
     4	both. A page is shared by reference count: a checkpoint holds the pages of the prefix it was taken at, and every
     5	sequence resumed from it holds them too.
     6	
     7	The pages fall in classes, one per card: the indexer's keys are split by position, so a sequence's logical page i
     8	must be a page of class i % classes (`include/engine_api.h`). Each class has its own free list and reservations.
     9	
    10	A sequence reserves, at admission, every page it can ever need (prompt plus `max_new`), and takes them one by one
    11	as it grows. So a running sequence never finds the pool empty.
    12	"""
    13	
    14	from __future__ import annotations
    15	
    16	from collections import deque
    17	from collections.abc import Sequence
    18	
    19	
    20	class PoolExhausted(RuntimeError):
    21	    pass
    22	
    23	
    24	type Counts = int | Sequence[int]
    25	"""Pages per class; an int for a pool of one class."""
    26	
    27	
    28	class PagePool:
    29	    def __init__(self, pages: int, classes: int = 1) -> None:
    30	        if pages <= 0:
    31	            raise ValueError("a pool needs at least one page")
    32	        if classes <= 0 or pages % classes:
    33	            raise ValueError(f"{pages} pages do not fall evenly in {classes} classes")
    34	        self.classes = classes
    35	        self._free: list[deque[int]] = [deque(range(k, pages, classes)) for k in range(classes)]
    36	        self._refs = [0] * pages
    37	        self._reserved = [0] * classes
    38	        self.size = pages
    39	
    40	    def _counts(self, n: Counts) -> list[int]:
    41	        if isinstance(n, int):
    42	            if self.classes != 1:
    43	                raise ValueError("a pool of several classes counts pages per class")
    44	            n = (n,)
    45	        if len(n) != self.classes or any(k < 0 for k in n):
    46	            raise ValueError(f"bad page counts {tuple(n)}")
    47	        return list(n)
    48	
    49	    def split(self, first: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    50	        """How many of the logical pages first .. end - 1 fall in each class."""
    51	        return tuple(len(range(first + (k - first) % self.classes, end, self.classes)) for k in range(self.classes))
    52	
    53	    @property
    54	    def free(self) -> int:
    55	        """Pages on the free lists, reserved or not."""
    56	        return sum(len(f) for f in self._free)
    57	
    58	    @property
    59	    def available(self) -> int:
    60	        """Pages that can still be reserved, summed over the classes."""
    61	        return self.free - self.reserved
    62	
    63	    @property
    64	    def reserved(self) -> int:
    65	        return sum(self._reserved)
    66	
    67	    def can_reserve(self, n: Counts) -> bool:
    68	        return all(k <= len(f) - r for k, f, r in zip(self._counts(n), self._free, self._reserved, strict=True))
    69	
    70	    def refs(self, page: int) -> int:
    71	        return self._refs[page]
    72	
    73	    def reserve(self, n: Counts) -> None:
    74	        counts = self._counts(n)
    75	        if not self.can_reserve(counts):
    76	            raise PoolExhausted(f"{tuple(counts)} pages wanted, {self.available} available")
    77	        for k, c in enumerate(counts):
    78	            self._reserved[k] += c
    79	
    80	    def unreserve(self, n: Counts) -> None:
    81	        counts = self._counts(n)
    82	        if any(c > r for c, r in zip(counts, self._reserved, strict=True)):
    83	            raise ValueError(f"unreserve {tuple(counts)} of {tuple(self._reserved)}")
    84	        for k, c in enumerate(counts):
    85	            self._reserved[k] -= c
    86	
    87	    def take(self, logical: int = 0) -> int:
    88	        """A page for logical page `logical`, from the caller's reservation, with one reference."""
    89	        k = logical % self.classes
    90	        if self._reserved[k] <= 0:
    91	            raise PoolExhausted("take without a reservation")
    92	        self._reserved[k] -= 1
    93	        page = self._free[k].popleft()
    94	        self._refs[page] = 1
    95	        return page
    96	
    97	    def incref(self, page: int) -> None:
    98	        if self._refs[page] <= 0:
    99	            raise ValueError(f"page {page} is free")
   100	        self._refs[page] += 1
   101	
   102	    def decref(self, page: int) -> None:
   103	        if self._refs[page] <= 0:
   104	            raise ValueError(f"page {page} is already free")
   105	        self._refs[page] -= 1
   106	        if self._refs[page] == 0:
   107	            self._free[page % self.classes].append(page)

1	"""The checkpoint pool: copies of a sequence's fixed state at a known prefix (DESIGN.md, section 4; ADR-0017).
     2	
     3	A shared prefix can reuse its KV pages, but the DeltaNet state only through a checkpoint taken where the prefix
     4	ends. A checkpoint here is the id of a state copy in the core, the tokens it was taken after, and the KV pages that
     5	cover those tokens (one reference each). Prefixes are keyed by the rendered tokens, never by text (ADR-0017,
     6	item 4).
     7	
     8	Eviction is least recently used. A kept checkpoint (the end of a long system prompt, ADR-0017 item 6) goes only
     9	when no other is left to evict.
    10	"""
    11	
    12	from __future__ import annotations
    13	
    14	import itertools
    15	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    16	
    17	from engine.seqstate.pages import PagePool
    18	
    19	
    20	@dataclass(slots=True)
    21	class Checkpoint:
    22	    id: int
    23	    tokens: tuple[int, ...]
    24	    pages: tuple[int, ...]
    25	    kept: bool
    26	    ready: bool = False
    27	    """The core has answered CHECKPOINT_DONE."""
    28	    used: int = 0
    29	    users: set[int] = field(default_factory=set[int])
    30	    """Slots being restored from it, which it must outlive until their restore is queued."""
    31	
    32	
    33	class CheckpointPool:
    34	    def __init__(self, size: int, pages: PagePool, max_kept: int = 2) -> None:
    35	        self._free = list(range(size - 1, -1, -1))
    36	        self._pages = pages
    37	        self._by_id: dict[int, Checkpoint] = {}
    38	        self._clock = itertools.count(1)
    39	        self.max_kept = max_kept
    40	        self.size = size
    41	
    42	    def __len__(self) -> int:
    43	        return len(self._by_id)
    44	
    45	    def __iter__(self):  # noqa: ANN204
    46	        return iter(self._by_id.values())
    47	
    48	    def get(self, checkpoint_id: int) -> Checkpoint | None:
    49	        return self._by_id.get(checkpoint_id)
    50	
    51	    def longest_prefix(self, prompt: tuple[int, ...]) -> Checkpoint | None:
    52	        """The ready checkpoint with the longest tokens that are a strict prefix of `prompt`."""
    53	        best: Checkpoint | None = None
    54	        for ck in self._by_id.values():
    55	            n = len(ck.tokens)
    56	            if not ck.ready or n >= len(prompt) or (best is not None and n <= len(best.tokens)):
    57	                continue
    58	            if prompt[:n] == ck.tokens:
    59	                best = ck
    60	        return best
    61	
    62	    def find(self, tokens: tuple[int, ...]) -> Checkpoint | None:
    63	        for ck in self._by_id.values():
    64	            if ck.tokens == tokens:
    65	                return ck
    66	        return None
    67	
    68	    def touch(self, ck: Checkpoint) -> None:
    69	        ck.used = next(self._clock)
    70	
    71	    def add(self, tokens: tuple[int, ...], pages: tuple[int, ...], kept: bool) -> tuple[Checkpoint, list[int]]:
    72	        """A new checkpoint holding a reference on each of `pages`, and the ids of any evicted to make room."""
    73	        evicted: list[int] = []
    74	        if kept and sum(ck.kept for ck in self._by_id.values()) >= self.max_kept:
    75	            kept_now = [ck for ck in self._by_id.values() if ck.kept]
    76	            min(kept_now, key=lambda c: c.used).kept = False
    77	        if not self._free:
    78	            victim = self.victim()
    79	            if victim is None:
    80	                raise RuntimeError("every checkpoint is in use")
    81	            evicted.append(victim.id)
    82	            self.remove(victim.id)
    83	        ck = Checkpoint(self._free.pop(), tokens, pages, kept)
    84	        for page in pages:
    85	            self._pages.incref(page)
    86	        self.touch(ck)
    87	        self._by_id[ck.id] = ck
    88	        return ck, evicted
    89	
    90	    def victim(self) -> Checkpoint | None:
    91	        """The checkpoint to evict next: the least recently used not in use, kept ones last."""
    92	        candidates = [ck for ck in self._by_id.values() if not ck.users and ck.ready]
    93	        if not candidates:
    94	            return None
    95	        return min(candidates, key=lambda c: (c.kept, c.used))
    96	
    97	    def remove(self, checkpoint_id: int) -> None:
    98	        ck = self._by_id.pop(checkpoint_id)
    99	        for page in ck.pages:
   100	            self._pages.decref(page)
   101	        self._free.append(ck.id)

   397	    def _run_span(self, slot: int, first: int, count: int, last: bool) -> int:

     2	
     3	It replays `reference/llamacpp-3cf0325-IQ3_S-greedy.jsonl`: the greedy tokens for each prompt of
     4	`reference/prompts.jsonl`. Behind the engine's interface it runs the same plans as the mock and checks them the same
     5	way, so the scheduler and the front end can run end to end against the model's real token ids. A prompt it has no
     6	record of fails with an ERROR event, and so does asking for more tokens than were recorded.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	from __future__ import annotations
    10	
    11	import json
    12	from collections.abc import Sequence
    13	from pathlib import Path
    14	
    15	from engine.api.mock import MockEngine
    16	
    17	REFERENCE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "reference"
    18	PROMPTS = REFERENCE_DIR / "prompts.jsonl"
    19	GREEDY = REFERENCE_DIR / "llamacpp-3cf0325-IQ3_S-greedy.jsonl"
    20	
    21	
    22	def load_reference(prompts: Path = PROMPTS, greedy: Path = GREEDY) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]:
    23	    """Each reference prompt's token ids, mapped to the greedy tokens llama.cpp produced for it."""
    24	    by_id: dict[str, tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    25	    with prompts.open() as f:
    26	        for line in f:
    27	            row = json.loads(line)
    28	            by_id[row["id"]] = tuple(row["tokens"])
    29	    out: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
    30	    with greedy.open() as f:
    31	        for line in f:
    32	            row = json.loads(line)
    33	            if "meta" in row:
    34	                continue
    35	            out[by_id[row["id"]]] = tuple(row["tokens"])
    36	    return out
    37	
    38	
    39	class ReferenceEngine(MockEngine):
    40	    def __init__(self, records: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] | None = None) -> None:
    41	        self._records = load_reference() if records is None else records
    42	        self._prompt_lengths = sorted({len(p) for p in self._records})
    43	        super().__init__(self._next)
    44	
    45	    def _next(self, tokens: Sequence[int]) -> int:
    46	        for n in self._prompt_lengths:
    47	            if n > len(tokens):
    48	                break
    49	            generated = self._records.get(tuple(tokens[:n]))
    50	            if generated is None:
    51	                continue
    52	            done = len(tokens) - n
    53	            if tuple(tokens[n:]) != generated[:done]:
    54	                raise KeyError("the sequence left the recorded tokens")
    55	            if done >= len(generated):
    56	                raise KeyError(f"only {len(generated)} tokens were recorded")
    57	            return generated[done]
    58	        raise KeyError("no recorded prompt is a prefix of this sequence")

    45	def tiny_tokenizer() -> Tokenizer:
    46	    """One token per byte (ids 0-255), then the special and added tokens: every UTF-8 character of more than one
    47	    byte spans several tokens, which is what the detokenizer must handle."""
    48	    alphabet = sorted(pre_tokenizers.ByteLevel.alphabet())
    49	    tokens = [*alphabet, *SPECIALS, *ADDED, *VISION]
    50	    types = [1] * len(alphabet) + [CONTROL] * len(SPECIALS) + [USER_DEFINED] * len(ADDED) + [CONTROL] * len(VISION)
    51	    return from_vocabulary(tokens, [], types)

    83	@dataclass
    84	class FakeEngine:
    85	    """The front end's view of an engine, answering every request with `output`, encoded with the tokenizer."""
    86	
    87	    tokenizer: Tokenizer
    88	    output: str = "Hello."
    89	    max_context: int = 4096
    90	    finish: protocol.Finish = protocol.Finish.STOP
    91	    eos: str | None = "<|im_end|>"
    92	    reused: int = 0
    93	    prompts: list[list[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: [])
    94	    max_news: list[int] = field(default_factory=lambda: [])
    95	    """The max_new each generation was given."""
    96	    stopped_early: int = 0
    97	    image_tokens_max: int = 0
    98	    images: list[list[PromptImage]] = field(default_factory=lambda: [])
    99	    status: str = "ready"
   100	    wake_error: str | None = None
   101	    sleeps: list[int] = field(default_factory=lambda: [])
   102	    """The drain each sleep was given, in ms."""
   103	    wakes: int = 0
   104	
   105	    @property
   106	    def info(self) -> dict[str, str]:
   107	        return {"backend": "fake"}
   108	
   109	    @property
   110	    def slots(self) -> int:
   111	        return 1
   112	
   113	    @property
   114	    def busy(self) -> int:
   115	        return 0
   116	
   117	    @property
   118	    def asleep(self) -> bool:
   119	        return self.status in ("loading", "sleeping", "asleep")
   120	
   121	    async def start(self) -> None:
   122	        pass
   123	
   124	    async def wake(self) -> dict[str, str]:
   125	        if self.wake_error is not None:
   126	            raise EngineUnavailable(self.wake_error)
   127	        self.wakes += 1
   128	        self.status = "ready"
   129	        return self.info
   130	
   131	    async def sleep(self, drain_ms: int) -> float:
   132	        self.sleeps.append(drain_ms)
   133	        self.status = "asleep"
   134	        return 1.5
   135	
   136	    async def close(self) -> None:
   137	        pass
   138	
   139	    async def generate(
   140	        self,
   141	        prompt: Sequence[int],
   142	        max_new: int,
   143	        settings: protocol.Settings,
   144	        images: Sequence[PromptImage] = (),
   145	    ) -> AsyncGenerator[protocol.Event]:
   146	        self.prompts.append(list(prompt))
   147	        self.max_news.append(max_new)
   148	        self.images.append(list(images))
   149	        ids = encode(self.tokenizer, self.output)
   150	        if self.eos is not None and self.finish is protocol.Finish.STOP:
   151	            eos = self.tokenizer.token_to_id(self.eos)
   152	            assert eos is not None
   153	            ids.append(eos)
   154	        ids = ids[:max_new]
   155	        finish = protocol.Finish.LENGTH if len(ids) == max_new and self.finish is protocol.Finish.STOP else self.finish
   156	        done = False
   157	        try:
   158	            if self.reused:
   159	                yield protocol.Resume(1, self.reused)
   160	            for i in ids:
   161	                yield protocol.Tokens(1, (i,))
   162	            done = True
   163	            yield protocol.Done(1, len(ids), len(prompt), 1.0, 2.0, finish, self.reused)
   164	        finally:
   165	            if not done:
   166	                self.stopped_early += 1

    35	def sse(text: str) -> list[tuple[str | None, Any]]:
    36	    out: list[tuple[str | None, Any]] = []
    37	    for block in text.strip().split("\n\n"):
    38	        event = None
    39	        data = None
    40	        for line in block.splitlines():
    41	            if line.startswith("event: "):
    42	                event = line[7:]
    43	            elif line.startswith("data: "):
    44	                data = line[6:]
    45	        assert data is not None
    46	        out.append((event, None if data == "[DONE]" else json.loads(data)))
    47	    return out

    20	def run_engine(lines: list[str], *args: str) -> list[protocol.Event]:
    21	    """Send the lines, read until each request has ended, then QUIT. (QUIT, or the pipe closing, ends the engine at
    22	    once, as when the front end goes away.)"""
    23	    argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "engine", "--backend", "mock", "--arch", "qwen4exp", *args]
    24	    p = subprocess.Popen(argv, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    25	    assert p.stdin is not None
    26	    assert p.stdout is not None
    27	    for line in lines:
    28	        p.stdin.write(line + "\n")
    29	    p.stdin.flush()
    30	    events: list[protocol.Event] = []
    31	    ended = 0
    32	    while ended < len(lines):
    33	        line = p.stdout.readline()
    34	        assert line, "the engine closed its output"
    35	        events.append(protocol.parse_event(line))
    36	        ended += isinstance(events[-1], (protocol.Done, protocol.Error))
    37	    p.stdin.write("QUIT\n")
    38	    p.stdin.close()
    39	    assert p.wait(timeout=30) == 0
    40	    return events

    85	    def __init__(self, *args: str) -> None:

   100	            assert line, "the engine closed its output"
   101	            out.append(protocol.parse_event(line))
   102	        return out

   106	        return self.p.wait(timeout=30)

    71	    cells: dict[int, list[int | None]] = field(default_factory=lambda: {})
    72	    """Each page's 4 cells: the token written at each position."""
    73	    page_plans: int = 0
    74	    """Plans that carried page changes."""
    75	    config: abi.CConfig | None = None
    76	    asleep: bool = False
    77	    error: str = ""
    78	    """What the next ERROR event reports through last_error."""

    80	    def open(self, config: abi.CConfig) -> abi.CInfo:
    81	        self.opened = (config.flags, config.mtp_dir)
    82	        self.config = config
    83	        return self._info(config)
    84	
    85	    def _info(self, config: abi.CConfig) -> abi.CInfo:
    86	        info = abi.CInfo()
    87	        info.api_version = abi.ABI_VERSION
    88	        info.cards = 2
    89	        info.slots = config.slots
    90	        info.max_ctx = config.max_ctx
    91	        info.prompt_chunk = self.prompt_chunk
    92	        info.checkpoints = config.checkpoints
    93	        info.max_step_rows = abi.MAX_STEP_SLOTS
    94	        info.image_tokens_max = self.image_tokens_max
    95	        self.max_ctx = config.max_ctx
    96	        self.npp = -(-config.max_ctx // 4 // self.cards) * self.cards
    97	        self.kv_pages = -(-config.kv_pages // self.cards) * self.cards if config.kv_pages else config.slots * self.npp
    98	        info.kv_pages = self.kv_pages
    99	        info.pages_per_slot = self.npp
   100	        return info

   102	    def admit(self, slot: int, settings: abi.CSettings, prompt: Sequence[int]) -> None:
   103	        assert slot not in self.slots, "admitted into a used slot"
   104	        assert all(
   105	            slot not in [p.slot for p in q.pieces[: q.npieces]] + list(q.slots[: q.nslots]) + [c.slot for c in pages]
   106	            for q, pages in self.plans
   107	        ), "admitted while a queued plan names the slot"
   108	        self.slots[slot] = _Slot(abi.CSettings.from_buffer_copy(settings), list(prompt))
   109	        self.table[slot] = []
   110	        self.queued_table[slot] = 0
   111	
   112	    def admit_images(self, slot: int, images: Sequence[Image]) -> None:
   113	        assert slot in self.slots, "images for a slot not admitted"
   114	        assert not self.slots[slot].tokens, "images after the slot began"
   115	        self.images[slot] = list(images)
   116	
   117	    def release(self, slot: int) -> None:
   118	        self.slots.pop(slot, None)
   119	        self.images.pop(slot, None)
   120	
   121	    def submit(self, plan: abi.CStepPlan) -> bool:
   122	        if len(self.plans) >= self.queue_limit:
   123	            return False
   124	        pages = [abi.CPageChange.from_buffer_copy(plan.pages[i]) for i in range(plan.npages)]
   125	        for c in pages:
   126	            mapped = self.queued_table.get(c.slot, 0)
   127	            assert c.logical <= mapped < self.npp + 1, f"logical page {c.logical} out of order ({mapped} mapped)"
   128	            if c.page == abi.NO_PAGE:
   129	                self.queued_table[c.slot] = c.logical
   130	                continue
   131	            assert c.page < self.kv_pages, f"page {c.page} past the pool"
   132	            assert c.page % self.cards == c.logical % self.cards, "page on the wrong card"
   133	            assert c.cells < 4
   134	            assert not c.cells or c.source % self.cards == c.page % self.cards, "copied from the wrong card"
   135	            if c.logical == mapped:
   136	                self.queued_table[c.slot] = mapped + 1
   137	        self.plans.append((abi.CStepPlan.from_buffer_copy(plan), pages))
   138	        return True
   139	
   140	    def _mapped(self, slot: int) -> int:
   141	        return 4 * len(self.table[slot])
   142	
   143	    def _stall(self, slot: int, s: _Slot) -> None:
   144	        if not s.stalled:
   145	            s.stalled = True
   146	            self._emit(abi.CEventKind.STALLED, slot, -1, len(s.tokens))
   147	
   148	    def _write(self, slot: int, s: _Slot, tokens: Sequence[int]) -> None:
   149	        for t in tokens:
   150	            pos = len(s.tokens)
   151	            self.cells.setdefault(self.table[slot][pos // 4], [None] * 4)[pos % 4] = t
   152	            s.tokens.append(t)
   153	
   154	    def _read(self, slot: int, n: int) -> list[int]:
   155	        """The slot's first n positions, read back through its page table, as attention reads them."""
   156	        out = [self.cells[self.table[slot][pos // 4]][pos % 4] for pos in range(n)]
   157	        assert None not in out, f"slot {slot} reads a cell never written"
   158	        return [t for t in out if t is not None]
   159	
   160	    def _apply(self, pages: Sequence[abi.CPageChange]) -> None:
   161	        self.page_plans += bool(pages)
   162	        for c in pages:
   163	            table = self.table[c.slot]
   164	            if c.page == abi.NO_PAGE:
   165	                del table[c.logical :]
   166	                continue
   167	            if c.cells:
   168	                self.cells.setdefault(c.page, [None] * 4)[: c.cells] = self.cells[c.source][: c.cells]
   169	            if c.logical == len(table):
   170	                table.append(c.page)
   171	            else:
   172	                table[c.logical] = c.page
   173	            if c.slot in self.slots:
   174	                self.slots[c.slot].stalled = False
   175	
   176	    def _emit(self, kind: abi.CEventKind, slot: int, token: int, value: int) -> None:
   177	        self.events.append(abi.CEvent(kind, slot, token, value))
   178	
   179	    def _produce(self, slot: int, s: _Slot) -> None:
   180	        tok = next_token(self._read(slot, len(s.tokens)))
   181	        s.next = tok
   182	        s.generated += 1
   183	        self._emit(abi.CEventKind.TOKEN, slot, tok, len(s.tokens))
   184	        stop = tok in list(s.settings.stop[: s.settings.n_stop])
   185	        if stop or s.generated >= s.settings.max_tokens:
   186	            s.done = True
   187	            self._emit(abi.CEventKind.DONE, slot, tok, abi.CDone.STOP if stop else abi.CDone.LENGTH)
   188	
   189	    def _run(self, plan: abi.CStepPlan, pages: Sequence[abi.CPageChange]) -> None:
   190	        self.seq += 1
   191	        self._apply(pages)
   192	        pieces = [(p.slot, p.tokens) for p in plan.pieces[: plan.npieces]]
   193	        self.log.append((pieces, list(plan.slots[: plan.nslots])))
   194	        for slot, n in pieces:
   195	            s = self.slots.get(slot)
   196	            if s is None or s.done or len(s.tokens) >= len(s.prompt):
   197	                continue
   198	            pos = len(s.tokens)
   199	            if self._mapped(slot) <= pos:
   200	                self._stall(slot, s)
   201	                continue
   202	            n = min(n or self.prompt_chunk, self.prompt_chunk, len(s.prompt) - pos, self._mapped(slot) - pos)
   203	            self._write(slot, s, s.prompt[pos : pos + n])
   204	            self.timing.append(abi.CTiming(abi.CTimingKind.PROMPT, self.seq, n, 0, 0, 1000 * n))
   205	            self._emit(abi.CEventKind.PROMPT, slot, -1, len(s.tokens))
   206	            if len(s.tokens) == len(s.prompt):
   207	                self._produce(slot, s)
   208	        rows = 0
   209	        for slot in plan.slots[: plan.nslots]:
   210	            s = self.slots.get(slot)
   211	            if s is None or s.done:
   212	                continue
   213	            assert len(s.tokens) >= len(s.prompt), "the core would read the prompt one token per step"
   214	            if self._mapped(slot) <= len(s.tokens):
   215	                self._stall(slot, s)
   216	                continue
   217	            self._write(slot, s, [s.next])
   218	            rows += 1
   219	            self._produce(slot, s)
   220	        if rows:
   221	            self.timing.append(abi.CTiming(abi.CTimingKind.DECODE, self.seq, rows, 0, 0, 10_000_000))
   222	        self._emit(abi.CEventKind.STEP, 0, -1, self.seq)
   223	
   224	    def _drain(self) -> None:
   225	        while self.plans:
   226	            self._run(*self.plans.popleft())
   227	
   228	    def poll(self, cap: int) -> list[abi.CEvent]:
   229	        if not self.events and self.plans:
   230	            self._run(*self.plans.popleft())
   231	        out: list[abi.CEvent] = []
   232	        while self.events and len(out) < cap:
   233	            out.append(self.events.popleft())
   234	        return out
   235	
   236	    def wait(self, timeout_ms: int) -> bool:
   237	        return bool(self.events or self.plans)
   238	
   239	    def checkpoint(self, slot: int, checkpoint_id: int) -> None:
   240	        self._drain()
   241	        self.checkpoints[checkpoint_id] = list(self.slots[slot].tokens)
   242	
   243	    def restore(self, slot: int, checkpoint_id: int) -> None:
   244	        self._drain()
   245	        s = self.slots[slot]
   246	        ck = self.checkpoints[checkpoint_id]
   247	        assert not s.tokens
   248	        assert len(ck) < len(s.prompt)
   249	        assert s.prompt[: len(ck)] == ck
   250	        s.tokens = list(ck)
   251	
   252	    def drop(self, checkpoint_id: int) -> None:
   253	        self.checkpoints.pop(checkpoint_id, None)
   254	
   255	    def read_timing(self, cap: int) -> list[abi.CTiming]:
   256	        out: list[abi.CTiming] = []
   257	        while self.timing and len(out) < cap:
   258	            out.append(self.timing.popleft())
   259	        return out
   260	
   261	    def sleep(self) -> None:
   262	        assert not self.slots, "asleep with a slot admitted"
   263	        assert not self.plans, "asleep with a plan queued"
   264	        self.checkpoints.clear()
   265	        self.table.clear()
   266	        self.queued_table.clear()
   267	        self.cells.clear()
   268	        self.asleep = True
   269	
   270	    def wake(self) -> abi.CInfo:
   271	        assert self.asleep
   272	        assert self.config is not None
   273	        self.asleep = False
   274	        return self._info(self.config)
   275	
   276	    def last_error(self) -> str:
   277	        return self.error
   278	
   279	    def close(self) -> None:
   280	        pass

   299	    def add(self, rid: int, prompt: Sequence[int], max_new: int, images: tuple[Image, ...] = ()) -> None:
   300	        gen = protocol.Gen(rid, max_new, tuple(prompt), protocol.Settings(temperature=0))

   303	    def until_idle(self, limit: int = 10_000) -> None:
   304	        for _ in range(limit):

   306	                return
   307	            self.events += self.scheduler.tick(0)
   308	        raise AssertionError("the scheduler did not finish")

   310	    def tokens(self, rid: int) -> list[int]:
   311	        return [t for e in self.events if isinstance(e, protocol.Tokens) and e.rid == rid for t in e.ids]
   312	
   313	    def done(self, rid: int) -> protocol.Done:
   314	        (d,) = [e for e in self.events if isinstance(e, protocol.Done) and e.rid == rid]
   315	        return d

The list's first command copies the step plan from host 404 memory to the card, and the kernels read that copy: a word read from host memory at each launch's start makes every 405 launch slower ([the record](MEASUREMENTS.md#2026-10-16-bf16-products-occupancy)). 406 407 ```mermaid 408 %%{init: {"theme": "base", "themeVariables": {"fontSize": "14px", "textColor": "#8b5cf6", "actorBkg": "#2e1065", "actorBorder": "#8b5cf6", "actorTextColor": "#ede9fe", "actorLineColor": "#8b5cf6", "signalColor": "#8b5cf6", "signalTextColor": "#8b5cf6", "labelBoxBkgColor": "#6d28d9", "labelBoxBorderColor": "#8b5cf6", "labelTextColor": "#ffffff", "loopTextColor": "#8b5cf6", "noteBkgColor": "#1f2433", "noteBorderColor": "#64748b", "noteTextColor": "#e2e8f0"}, "sequence": {"mirrorActors": false}}}%% 409 sequenceDiagram 410 box rgba(100,116,139,0.12) HOST 411 participant W as CPU workers 412 participant H as Engine thread 413 end 414 box rgba(0,113,197,0.12) ARC PRO B60 × 2 415 participant A as Card 0 416 participant B as Card 1 417 end 418 419 Note over H: embed the rows, write the step plan 420 H->>A: run the recorded list 421 H->>B: run the recorded list 422 Note over H: read the n-gram rows, cache or SSD 423 H-->>A: event: n-gram rows ready 424 H-->>B: event: n-gram rows ready 425 loop each of the 48 layers 426 Note over A,B: mix · token mixer

1	# Testing
     2	
     3	This page says how each part of the engine is checked, against what, where, and how long a check may take.
     4	[ADR-0012](adr/0012-correctness-reference.md) fixes the reference: llama.cpp's CPU backend at `3cf0325`, through
     5	the reference outputs ([REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md](REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md)). The tools are
     6	[ADR-0004](adr/0004-write-or-reuse.md)'s: `pytest` for every test, `numpy` to compare tensors, and plain executables
     7	under `ctest` for the core's own unit tests.
     8	
     9	Level Zero has no CPU device, so every test of a kernel runs on a B60 ([ADR-0001](adr/0001-level-zero-from-scratch.md)).
    10	"The machine" below is the test machine of [MEASUREMENTS.md#the-test-machine](MEASUREMENTS.md#the-test-machine).
    11	
    12	## The levels
    13	
    14	| Level | What it checks | Reference | Where it runs | Time budget |
    15	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    16	| 1. Host | Python: the scheduler, admission, sequence-state bookkeeping, the memory plan, the GGUF tensor table, the protocol, the front end against the mock engine ([ADR-0022](adr/0022-two-processes-python-and-cpp.md)). C++: layouts shared across the C ABI, ring buffers, the arena's free list | expected values written in the test; the C ABI's struct sizes and offsets checked from both sides | anywhere, no card | 30 s |
    17	| 2. Wrapper | each function of [ADR-0003](adr/0003-kernel-language.md)'s header of Intel builtins (block reads, DPAS, sub-group shuffles), once | expected results written in the test, as the kernel spike checked them ([record](MEASUREMENTS.md#2026-10-11-kernel-spike)) | the machine | 1 min |
    18	| 3. Kernel | each kernel against reference values for the same inputs: every expert type's decode, the dense products, DeltaNet, attention, the indexer, norms, sampling | ggml's CPU implementation of the same operation (its `to_float` dequantisation and dot products, called from the test through the pinned ggml), or a scalar reference in double precision inside the test. A generator kept in the repository is test code, owned like engine code | the machine | 5 min |
    19	| 4. Layer | a whole block of the model fed fixed inputs; the image encoder is the only one checked | llama.cpp's rows for the same images ([record](MEASUREMENTS.md#2026-10-17-encoder-reference)) | the machine | 10 min |
    20	| 5. End to end | the tokenizer; greedy agreement, teacher-forced and free-running; mean KL and top-1 agreement on the KL text | the reference prompts, greedy tokens and KL base ([REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md](REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md)) | the machine | 30 min |
    21	| 6. Determinism | a request's tokens are identical alone, in a window, batched, and packed with other prompts, with [ADR-0016](adr/0016-how-a-change-is-judged.md)'s switches set: no PCIe share of the misses, no adaptive swaps, no prefetching, no prompt cache. Also two runs of the same request, and runs with the CPU's misses on 8 and 16 workers | the engine's own run alone | the machine | 30 min |
    22	| 7. Performance | accepted tokens per window and wall time per window ([ADR-0016](adr/0016-how-a-change-is-judged.md)); decode tokens/s and prompt tokens/s at 4K against [ADR-0019](adr/0019-performance-target.md)'s target and the latest measurements | [MEASUREMENTS.md](MEASUREMENTS.md); before and after alternate (ABBA) on fresh processes, 3 rounds, medians and ranges ([MEASUREMENTS.md#how-the-numbers-were-taken](MEASUREMENTS.md#how-the-numbers-were-taken)) | the machine, in the measurement state of MEASUREMENTS.md#how-the-numbers-were-taken step 1 | ~30 min |
    23	
    24	The tests that exist, by level (each is described in [DEVELOPING.md](DEVELOPING.md#tests)):
    25	
    26	- Level 1: the Python host tests in `tests/host/`, and `gguf_test` and `mrope_test`. No ring-buffer or free-list test.
    27	- Level 2: `ze_smoke_test`, `topk_test` and `gemm_test`'s DPAS layout check. Not every builtin has a test.
    28	- Level 3: `matvec_test`, `moe_test`, `gemm_test`, `qgemm_test`, `attn_test` and `vision_test`.
    29	- Level 4: `encoder_test`. No test of a text layer exists.
    30	- Level 5: `greedy_test` (teacher-forced), `api_test` and the tokenizer check in `tests/end_to_end/`. No free-running
    31	  or KL check.
    32	- Level 6: `batch_test`, and `api_test`'s drafting and swap cases. The packed, two-run and worker-count cases are not
    33	  built.
    34	
    35	Levels 1-3 run on every change. Levels 4-6 run on every change to a kernel, the decode loop, the memory system or the
    36	scheduler. Level 7 runs on every change that claims speed.
    37	
    38	Level 7 is valid only after level 6 passes: a faster run that changes tokens is a different computation. So level 7
    39	fails a change that is faster but lowers acceptance. A change fails if its median wall time per window is worse than
    40	before by more than the range of the "before" runs, or if accepted tokens per window fall at all with the switches
    41	set. Its record says which of the two failed.
    42	
    43	## Tolerances
    44	
    45	The error measure for a tensor is the largest absolute difference divided by the largest absolute reference value,
    46	unless a row says otherwise.
    47	
    48	| Path | Tolerance | Why |
    49	| --- | --- | --- |
    50	| Integer work: decoding a quantised block to its integers, int8 dot products before scaling | exact | Integer arithmetic has one right answer |
    51	| FP32 results from quantised or BF16 weights (the decode kernels, with the same activations the reference is given) | 1e-5 | Only the order of the float sums differs from the reference. The kernel spike's kernels met 1.0e-7 to 1.4e-7 for all eight types ([record](MEASUREMENTS.md#2026-10-11-kernel-spike)) |
    52	| FP16 products on the XMX units (the prompt path) | 2e-3 | fp16 carries 11 bits (a rounding of 4.9e-4 per value). The prompt kernels of the design-inputs record, the fp16 ones included, met 1e-7 to 3e-4 ([design-inputs record, part 8](MEASUREMENTS.md#2026-10-13-design-inputs)) |
    53	| BF16 outputs (the image encoder's kernels that write a product's next input, [MODEL_VISION.md](spec/MODEL_VISION.md)) | 1e-2 | bf16 carries 8 bits (a rounding of 3.9e-3 per value), on top of the fp16 error where the inputs are fp16 |
    54	| The DeltaNet recurrence over 2,048 tokens, FP32 state | 1e-5 | Checked against double precision in the same run of the design-inputs record; the state does not grow (its gate is below 1) |
    55	| End to end, the KL text | mean KL at most 0.02, top-1 agreement at least 95% | 0.02 is ADR-0012's gate. The reference against itself gives 99.99% top-1, and 0.035 KL / 91% when only llama.cpp's batch size changes ([REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md](REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md#what-changes-it)), so the engine feeds the KL text in 512-token pieces for this check. *Provisional*: to be revisited with the first measurement |
    56	| End to end, greedy, teacher-forced | at least 95% of positions, on the prompts of up to 512 tokens | Those are the most reliable references ([REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md](REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md#which-greedy-outputs-to-trust)); longer prompts are reported, not gated |
    57	
    58	## Test data
    59	
    60	| Data | Where | How a test finds it |
    61	| --- | --- | --- |
    62	| Small vectors (a few KB): wrapper expectations, hand-made kernel inputs | committed, beside the tests | relative path |
    63	| The reference prompts and greedy tokens | committed, `reference/` | relative path |
    64	| The KL base (8.1 GB) | not distributed; made as [REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md](REFERENCE_OUTPUTS.md) says | `FLASH_REF_DIR` |
    65	| The encoder's reference rows | the machine, `$FLASH_REF_DIR/vision` ([record](MEASUREMENTS.md#2026-10-17-encoder-reference)) | `FLASH_REF_DIR` |
    66	| The model | the machine, `/models` in the container ([MODEL_FILES.md](MODEL_FILES.md)) | `FLASH_MODEL_DIR`, defaulting to `/models` |
    67	
    68	**A test whose data is missing, or whose sha256 does not match, skips with a message naming the file. It never
    69	passes** ([ADR-0012](adr/0012-correctness-reference.md), decision 5). A run that skipped tests reports how many.
    70	
    71	## Where tests run
    72	
    73	- Anywhere, without a card: level 1, and compiling every kernel with `ocloc` when the
    74	  container is at hand.
    75	- On a machine with two B60s, in the engine image ([ADR-0025](adr/0025-the-engine-image.md)): levels 2-7.
    76	  GPU tests carry the ctest label `gpu`. A GPU test skips when Level Zero lists no GPU, and fails instead when
    77	  `ENGINE_EXPECT_GPUS` is set, so a run on the cards sets it.
    78	- CI, on GitHub's hosted runners ([ADR-0028](adr/0028-ci-without-a-card.md)), on every push: it builds the image,
    79	  the engine and every kernel, runs the Python checks and level 1, and checks that every GPU test of the core skips
    80	  without a card and fails without one when `ENGINE_EXPECT_GPUS` is set. No self-hosted runner with the cards is set
    81	  up, so levels 2-6 run by hand.
    82	
    83	## The rule for every kernel change
    84	
    85	A change that adds or changes a kernel:
    86	
    87	1. adds its level-3 test, against ggml or a scalar reference, at the shapes the model uses, and with the tolerance of
    88	   its type above;
    89	2. runs the level 4-6 tests that exist and says they passed;
    90	3. if it claims speed, runs level 7 and links its row in [MEASUREMENTS.md](MEASUREMENTS.md);
    91	4. shows in its commit message the commands run, the counts passed and skipped, and the largest error per test.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file from the repository and return its contents with line numbers. Reads up to 2,000 lines by default; use offset and limit for longer files.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to read

offset.description: First line to return, 1-based; defaults to 1

limit.description: Number of lines to return; defaults to 2000

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create a file or overwrite an existing one with the given contents. Creates parent directories as needed.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to write

content.description: The whole contents of the file

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace one occurrence of old_string in a file with new_string. old_string must match the file exactly, whitespace included, and must occur exactly once unless replace_all is true.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to edit

new_string.description: The text to put in its place

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence; defaults to false

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List the files and directories directly inside a directory. Directories end with a slash. Entries ignored by .gitignore are left out unless include_ignored is true.

path.description: Absolute path of the directory

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose path matches a glob pattern, such as src/**/*.py. Returns absolute paths, newest first.

pattern.description: The glob pattern, relative to path

path.description: Directory to search in; defaults to the working directory

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a regular expression. Returns file path, line number and the matching line, at most 250 lines. Respects .gitignore.

path.description: File or directory to search; defaults to the working directory

include.description: Only files matching this glob, such as *.py

context.description: Lines of context before and after each match

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run one shell command in the working directory and return its combined stdout and stderr, truncated at 30,000 characters, with the exit code. The command is killed at the timeout.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds before the command is killed; defaults to 120000, at most 600000

description.description: What the command does, in a few words, shown to the user

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Run the repository's tests and return the summary line and each failure with its traceback. Detects pytest, cargo, go test, npm test and ctest from the repository's files unless command is given.

command.description: The test command to run instead of the detected one

filter.description: Run only tests whose name matches; passed to the runner's own filter option

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Return the current branch and the working tree status in short form, read-only.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Return the diff of the working tree against the index, or against a ref if given, read-only.

ref.description: A commit, branch or tag to diff against

path.description: Limit the diff to this path

staged.description: Diff the index against HEAD instead

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Replace the task list shown to the user. Each item has a short description and a status.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Stop and ask the user a question. Use only when the answer changes what you do next. Returns their reply.

options.description: Short choices to offer; the user may answer freely
